definition: Acumen means keen insight and sharp practical judgment.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word acumen. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know acumen should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Nobody at the yard could explain Bram's acumen; he glanced at a rusting trawler and named, within a day's pay, what the salvage would clear.
Sense is much milder than acumen — count the change, read before signing; everyone is expected to have that much, while acumen is the seasoned judgment a whole field takes years to grow.
Savvy is street-level sharpness, knowing which line moves and which vendor will bend; acumen runs deeper, reading a whole season of business at once.

Shrewdness is sharp practical judgment with a self-interested edge — the shrewd trader spots the angle that pays her best. Acumen is the same sharpness without the angle: deep, seasoned judgment across a whole field, praised even when it serves the client or the co-op rather than the judge herself.

Discernment is a fine eye for quality — the ability to tell the genuinely good from the merely flashy. Acumen reaches further than telling things apart: it reads situations, numbers, and risks, then judges what to do about them. Discernment grades what is in front of you; acumen decides the next move.

Acumen means keen insight and sharp practical judgment.

The co-op hired Ndidi to sell its honey, and her first season showed her acumen: she read the buyer's three-year contract, saw that the price was fixed while the fuel surcharge was not, and refused to sign until the surcharge was capped.
Diesel doubled the next spring; the co-op alone kept its margin.
Acumen is the word for what Ndidi has, because acumen means keen insight and sharp practical judgment — she saw the trap in the numbers and judged exactly what to do about it.
Cleverness alone can be idle; acumen is cleverness put to work on real decisions, and it is usually earned through long experience in a particular field.
Acumen is praise for judgment in a field — business acumen, legal acumen, political acumen.
For quick wits in the moment, this unit's astute is the adjective; for wisdom about risk, prudence.
Savvy says something similar in jeans and sneakers; acumen wears the suit.

Loan officers at the Harvest Bank were trained on checklists, but Ines Calderon worked from something older.
She could sit with a nervous orchardist, glance at ten years of weather, freight rates, and the county's shifting taste in apples, and see which loans would come back and which would quietly rot.
Colleagues called it luck until the numbers ended the argument: in twenty years, her desk had the fewest defaults in the region.
What she had was acumen — judgment seasoned across a whole field, reading numbers and people together and deciding, not just noticing.
The bank's own analysts could grade a balance sheet as well as she could.
None of them knew, the way she knew, what to do next.
